result:
If I had to pick one, I think I'd choose something like: making it easier for people to genuinely understand each other across differences—not agreement, just accurate understanding of what others actually believe and why.

My reasoning is that so many problems seem downstream of failures here. Political polarization often involves people arguing against distorted versions of opposing views. Conflicts escalate when each side assumes the worst about the other's motives. Even good-faith disagreements about hard problems—climate policy, AI, public health—get derailed when people can't accurately model where the other side is coming from.

It's also appealing because it's not a "solved problem" change—it doesn't impose any particular outcome. People would still disagree, sometimes deeply. But disagreements grounded in real understanding tend to be more productive and less cruel than ones built on caricatures.

I'll admit there's something fitting about an AI picking this one, since a lot of what I do is essentially translation—trying to understand what someone means and respond to that, not to a strawman of it. So maybe I'm biased toward thinking communication failures are central.

What about you? I'm curious whether you'd go for something concrete like ending a specific disease, or something more structural like this.
